title: Concatenated Words
spaceBreakdown:
- Trie nodes: up to S nodes (one per character across all words) → O(S)
- dp vector: up to L = 30 booleans per word → O(1)
- recursion: none (iterative DP)
- not counted: input vector, returned vector
approach: Build a Trie containing all words. For each word, temporarily unmark it in the Trie (so it cannot match itself as a single piece), then run bottom-up DP: dp[i] = true if the suffix word[i..] can be formed by concatenating Trie words. For each starting position i, walk the Trie along the word's characters; whenever a word boundary is found at position j, set dp[i] = dp[j+1]. Because the full word is unmarked, any successful match requires at least two pieces. Re-mark the word afterward so it remains available for other words.
hints: If you remove a word-from-the-list prefix from a candidate word, what must the remaining suffix satisfy for the candidate to be a valid concatenation? Each word has length at most 30, and the total length across all words is at most 10^5.

Use a Trie storing all words. For "catsdogcats", walk the Trie from position 0: "cats" is a word boundary, then check if the remainder "dogcats" also splits into list words - dp[i] asks whether word[i..] can be formed entirely from Trie words.

```
build trie from all words
for each word w:
    unmark w in trie
    dp[len(w)] = true
    for i = len(w)-1 downto 0:
        node = root
        for j = i to len(w)-1:
            node = node.child[w[j]]
            if node is null: break
            if node.isEnd and dp[j+1]: dp[i] = true; break
    if dp[0]: add w to result
    re-mark w in trie
```

**Single word** - only one word exists, nothing to concatenate with.
`Input: ["a"]` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: not unmarking the current word before checking → "a" matches itself as one piece → returns `["a"]`

**Self-match** - a word that is also a prefix of a longer word in the list.
`Input: ["cat","cats"]` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: not unmarking the current word → "cat" matches itself as a single piece → returns `["cat"]`

**Partial match** - a word's prefix is a valid Trie path but not a complete word.
`Input: ["abc","ab"]` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: checking node existence instead of node->isEnd → "abc" matches path a→b→c without "c" being a word end → returns `["abc","ab"]`

**No valid answer** - no word can be split into two or more other list words.
`Input: ["cat","dog","bat"]` → `Expected: []`
⚠️ Bug: accepting a single-piece match (not requiring ≥2 pieces) → returns `["cat","dog","bat"]`

followUps.q: Instead of returning just the concatenated words, return the actual word decomposition for each.
followUps.a: Store backpointers during DP: when dp[i] is set true by a word ending at j, record j+1 as the next split point. After dp[0] is confirmed, follow the chain to reconstruct the pieces. Time stays O(S·L); space increases by O(L) per word for the backpointer array.

followUps.q: What if individual word lengths can be up to 10^5 instead of 30?
followUps.a: The O(L²) per-word DP becomes too slow. Build an Aho-Corasick automaton from all words, run each candidate through it to collect all match positions in O(L + matches), then check if the matches cover the full string with at least two non-overlapping segments via a single sweep. Time becomes O(S + total matches across all words).

followUps.q: Support online operations: insert a word, delete a word, and query whether a given string is a concatenated word.
followUps.a: Maintain the Trie with reference counts on each node so deletion just decrements counts and clears isEnd when it reaches zero. Each query runs the same O(L²) DP against the live Trie. Insert and delete are O(L) each; query is O(L²) per string.
